Regularized linear deconvolution of BOLD time series

Source: R/deconvolve_reglin.R
deconvolve_reglin.Rd

Estimate a continuous latent activity time series by solving a regularized inverse convolution problem for one or more BOLD signals.

Usage

deconvolve_reglin(
  BOLDobs,
  kernel,
  lambda = NULL,
  lambda_grid = 10^seq(-4, 2, length.out = 20),
  penalty = c("diff2", "diff1", "ridge", "matern1", "sobolev"),
  kernel_grid = NULL,
  hrf_lags = 0L,
  tune_by = c("global", "signal"),
  normalize = TRUE,
  demean = TRUE,
  trim_kernel = TRUE,
  ridge_floor = 1e-08,
  return_diagnostics = FALSE,
  prewhiten_gcv = FALSE,
  prewhiten_rho = NULL,
  backend = c("cpp", "r", "wiener"),
  wiener_shrinkage = c("scalar", "psd"),
  wiener_psd_smooth = 7L,
  wiener_psd_floor = 1e-08,
  gcv_rule = c("min", "1se"),
  scaling = NULL
)

Arguments

BOLDobs

matrix of observed BOLD time series (n_timepoints x n_signals) or a numeric vector.

kernel

assumed HRF kernel. A vector or single-column matrix.

lambda

regularization strength. If NULL, chosen from lambda_grid by generalized cross-validation.

lambda_grid

candidate regularization strengths used when lambda is NULL.

penalty

regularization penalty: "diff2" for smooth second differences, "diff1" for smooth first differences, "ridge" for amplitude shrinkage, "matern1" for a damped first-order Matérn penalty, or "sobolev" for a critically damped second-order Sobolev penalty.

kernel_grid

optional list or matrix of candidate HRF kernels. If supplied, kernel and hrf_lags are ignored for tuning.

hrf_lags

integer shifts, in TR bins, applied to kernel. Negative values make the candidate HRF peak earlier; positive values make it later.

tune_by

whether to tune lambda/HRF globally across all signals or independently for each signal.

normalize

whether to z-score BOLDobs before deconvolution. Default: TRUE.

demean

whether to subtract column means before deconvolution. Ignored when normalize = TRUE, because z-scoring already demeans.

trim_kernel

whether to remove the initial length(kernel) - 1 latent samples, corresponding to pre-observation HRF support.

ridge_floor

small diagonal ridge added for numerical stability.

return_diagnostics

whether to return a list containing diagnostics rather than only the deconvolved matrix.

prewhiten_gcv

whether to estimate AR(1) autocorrelation and use a prewhitened objective for lambda/HRF selection and deconvolution.

prewhiten_rho

optional AR(1) coefficient used when prewhiten_gcv = TRUE. If NULL, a pooled median AR(1) coefficient is estimated from first-pass reconstruction residuals.

backend

implementation backend. "cpp" uses the RcppArmadillo regularized inverse implementation; "r" uses the reference R implementation; "wiener" uses a frequency-domain Wiener-style deconvolution for comparison.

wiener_shrinkage

shrinkage strategy for backend = "wiener". "scalar" uses Conj(H) / (|H|^2 + lambda). "psd" estimates smoothed signal and residual noise spectra from a scalar Wiener first pass, then uses frequency-dependent shrinkage.

wiener_psd_smooth

odd integer smoothing width for the estimated signal/noise spectra in wiener_shrinkage = "psd".

wiener_psd_floor

lower bound for estimated spectra.

gcv_rule

lambda/HRF selection rule. "min" selects the minimum mean GCV candidate. "1se" selects the largest lambda whose mean GCV is within one standard error of the minimum. The standard error is computed across signal columns for tune_by = "global".

scaling

Explicit input scaling: "zscore", "noise_sd", "demean", "none", or "psc" (percent signal change). When supplied, overrides normalize and demean. Otherwise those flags retain their existing behavior; the default is z-scoring.

Value

A matrix of deconvolved time series, or a list with activity and tuning diagnostics when return_diagnostics = TRUE.

Details

Constant signals and signals containing nonfinite observations are excluded from fitting and tuning. Their activity columns are returned as NA; diagnostics include a per-column signal_status vector ("ok", "constant", or "nonfinite"). Partial missingness excludes the entire signal; observations are not interpolated or deleted.

Z-scoring remains the default and is recommended for standardized within-run trial responses. For fixed HRF/regularization, the linear inverse is homogeneous in its input: rescaling the observations rescales activity without changing the conditioning of the inverse matrix. Without z-scoring, global GCV gives signals with larger variance more weight. Demeaning retains input units; "none" retains offsets too and is mainly useful for already-centered data or simulations. Percent signal change uses 100 * (y - mean(y)) / mean(y) and requires a positive baseline well away from zero. It is unsuitable for zero-mean residuals. No scaling choice removes HRF uncertainty or regularization-induced attenuation.

Scaling is applied once. The matrix attributes scaled:center, scaled:scale, and scaling record the actual BOLD transformation (y - center) / scale; diagnostics expose the same values. With scaling = "none", the recorded center is zero. The activity scale depends on this transformation and the unit-sum HRF; it is not a calibrated physiological neural-amplitude scale. The removed BOLD mean is not an identified neural baseline.

Scalar Wiener GCV uses the exact trace of the finite observed smoother, including zero extension, latent truncation, and the implemented filtered HRF when whitening. This trace is conditional on preprocessing and the AR(1) coefficient; it does not include derivatives of estimated preprocessing/noise parameters. Adaptive PSD shrinkage requires a fixed lambda and a single HRF. Its diagnostics label the filter trace conditional_fixed_psd and return missing GCV values, because the trace holding spectra fixed is not the degrees of freedom of the full nonlinear, data-adaptive estimator. Scalar diagnostics use df_method = "finite_observation_trace".
